assessment.nobel_worthiness: A theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic twist angles followed by the experimental discovery of correlated insulator and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene opened a new field of tunable moire quantum matter. The idea is original, simple to state and has a very large downstream impact.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model supplied the prediction and the Jarillo-Herrero group's 2018 experiments the decisive demonstration. Together they form a clean theory-plus-experiment configuration. Others (for example the Cao and Fatemi co-authors and early graphene-twist work) are not in the credited list, so the fairness of a three-person split is somewhat open.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many groups across several moire platforms within about eight years. The core physics is stable, although the nature of the superconductivity is still debated; recognition is timely for the discovery itself.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene is unresolved.
Other contributors to the experimental discovery may deserve credit beyond the three names listed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The observation of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the later identification of TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 as sources created neutrino astronomy. Building a cubic-kilometre Cherenkov detector in Antarctic ice was a major experimental achievement with clear lasting scientific consequence. I judge this as an experimentalist familiar with astroparticle instrumentation.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the IceCube project as principal investigator. Karle has been a senior leader of the detector and analysis effort. Spiering is also credited but I regard his role as less clearly decisive. The collaboration is large, which makes a three-person limit difficult and the allocation contestable. I make no claim to have independently verified internal roles.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is established at high significance and has been checked with different channels. Source associations are at a few-sigma level and the origin of most events is still unknown, but the discovery itself is mature and stable.
uncertainties: Individual credit within a large collaboration is hard to assign fairly.
Source identifications remain statistically modest and the bulk origin of the flux is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The proposal of magic-wavelength trapping and its realization in optical lattice clocks have taken timekeeping to fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. The invention is original and clear, and it enables tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a likely redefinition of the second.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and built the first strontium lattice clock. Ye brought it to the highest accuracy and stability. The two-person configuration is natural, though Hall, Hansch and others earlier received recognition for the optical frequency comb that underpins these clocks.
assessment.maturity: Multiple independent labs reproduce and compare clocks at the 1e-18 level. The redefinition of the SI second is still pending, so formal impact is still developing, but the technology is mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes for optical frequency combs and ion clocks may affect how the committee views novelty.
Other lattice-clock pioneers might merit consideration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by the observation of helical edge transport in HgTe quantum wells, established a major paradigm in condensed matter. The idea is conceptually deep and the experiments are decisive.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the key theoretical prediction and introduced the Z2 classification, and Molenkamp's group delivered the experimental realization (following the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal). The omission of Bernevig and Hughes from the credited list complicates a fully fair allocation, and Shoucheng Zhang's death removes one possible laureate.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed in HgTe, InAs/GaSb and three-dimensional materials, with strong follow-on work. The topic is mature and well understood, so recognition is timely.
uncertainties: The BHZ proposal is not in the credited names, so the credit allocation is partial.
Some topological claims, such as Majorana applications, remain unsettled but are not part of this discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Realizing Hubbard-model physics, the superfluid to Mott-insulator transition and fermionic correlated states with ultracold atoms in optical lattices gave a controllable quantum simulator of many-body physics. The work is influential across atomic and condensed-matter physics.
assessment.attribution: Greiner and Bloch carried out the Mott-insulator experiments and later quantum gas microscopy, and Esslinger led the fermionic Hubbard work. Zoller is credited as a theory pioneer but also appears in other candidates. The three experimentalists form a plausible set, but the exclusion of Zoller needs consideration.
assessment.maturity: Well replicated worldwide, with the field maturing toward quantitative simulation of problems out of reach of classical computation. The scientific payoff is still growing, which makes timing reasonable but not urgent.
uncertainties: Theory credit (Zoller, Jaksch) would be left out of this allocation.
The scope is broad, with overlap with the other quantum-simulation candidates on the list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution gives cryptography whose security rests on physical law and is a clear conceptual and practical application of quantum measurement. It has spawned a large field of quantum communication including satellite links.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard proposed BB84 and Ekert proposed the entanglement-based protocol, which is a natural three-way configuration. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Experimental demonstrations are mature and commercial systems exist, but practical security against real-device side channels is a continuing concern. The foundational ideas are clear and long confirmed. Part of this area adjoins the 2022 prize on entanglement.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 prize and the role of Wiesner may complicate attribution.
Real-world security depends on engineering considerations that are not fundamental physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* were a landmark of precision measurement, combining very-long-baseline interferometry with a global array. They directly test strong-field gravity and accretion physics and carry a strong public impact.
assessment.attribution: Falcke proposed imaging the shadow, Doeleman led the building and direction of the EHT, and Moran contributed to the technical foundation of mm-VLBI. The EHT collaboration comprises hundreds of people, so naming three laureates is unavoidably selective.
assessment.maturity: The results are only a few years old and confirmed mostly within the same collaboration, though with repeat observations and multiple epochs. Interpretation of the images in terms of black-hole parameters depends on modelling. The 2020 prize already recognized black-hole physics.
uncertainties: Independent confirmation outside the collaboration is limited.
Attribution within a very large collaboration is contentious.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of a bright millisecond radio burst of extragalactic origin opened a new astrophysical transient class, later shown to include repeaters and a Galactic magnetar burst. It is a clear observational discovery with cosmological uses for baryon census work.
assessment.attribution: Lorimer, McLaughlin and Bailes reported the first burst in 2007 and are credited. Thornton and others who showed they were a population, and the CHIME and ASKAP teams that localized them, are not credited, so a fair allocation is not straightforward.
assessment.maturity: Hundreds to thousands of bursts have been seen with independent facilities and host galaxies identified, so the phenomenon is confirmed. The physical origin remains unsettled, which leaves the prize more observational than explanatory and perhaps somewhat early.
uncertainties: The source mechanism is not understood.
The first burst was initially questioned, and later teams strengthened the case, so credit is distributed.
